037/**
038 *  Contains useful utilities for some common HTTP tasks.
039 *
040 *  @since 2.1.61.

042public final class HttpUtil {
043
044    private static final Logger LOG = LogManager.getLogger( HttpUtil.class );
045    private static final int    ONE                   = 48;
046    private static final int    NINE                  = 57;
047    private static final int    DOT                   = 46;
048    
049    /** Private constructor to prevent direct instantiation. */
050    private HttpUtil() {
051    }
052    
053    /**
054     * returns the remote address by looking into {@code x-forwarded-for} header or, if unavailable, 
055     * into {@link HttpServletRequest#getRemoteAddr()}.
056     * 
057     * @param req http request
058     * @return remote address associated to the request.
059     */
060    public static String getRemoteAddress( final HttpServletRequest req ) {
061        String realIP = StringUtils.isNotEmpty ( req.getHeader( "X-Forwarded-For" ) ) ? req.getHeader( "X-Forwarded-For" ) :
062                                                                                          req.getRemoteAddr();
063        // can be a comma-separated list of IPs
064        if (realIP.contains(","))
065                realIP = realIP.substring(realIP.indexOf(","));
066
067        return realIP;
068    
069    }
070
071    /**
072     * Returns whether or not the IP address of the request equals a given IP,
073     * or is in a given IP range
074     *
075     * @param req http request
076     * @param ipOrRange IP address or IP range to test against
077     * @since 3.0.0
078     * @return
079     */
080    public static boolean ipIsInRange(final HttpServletRequest req, final String ipOrRange) {
081        String requestIP = getRemoteAddress(req);
082        if (ipOrRange.contains("/")) {
083            SubnetUtils subnet = new SubnetUtils(ipOrRange);
084            SubnetUtils.SubnetInfo subnetInfo = subnet.getInfo();
085            return subnetInfo.isInRange(requestIP);
086        } else {
087            return requestIP.equals(ipOrRange);
088        }
089    }
090
091    /**
092     *  Attempts to retrieve the given cookie value from the request. Returns the string value (which may or may not be decoded
093     *  correctly, depending on browser!), or null if the cookie is not found. The algorithm will automatically trim leading
094     *  and trailing double quotes, if found.
095     *
096     *  @param request The current request
097     *  @param cookieName The name of the cookie to fetch.
098     *  @return Value of the cookie, or null, if there is no such cookie.
099     */
100    public static String retrieveCookieValue( final HttpServletRequest request, final String cookieName ) {
101        final Cookie[] cookies = request.getCookies();
102        if( cookies != null ) {
103            for( final Cookie cookie : cookies ) {
104                if( cookie.getName().equals( cookieName ) ) {
105                    String value = cookie.getValue();
106                    if( value == null || value.isEmpty() ) {
107                        return null;
108                    }
109                    if( value.charAt( 0 ) == '"' && value.charAt( value.length() - 1 ) == '"' ) {
110                        value = value.substring( 1, value.length() - 1 );
111                    }
112                    return value;
113                }
114            }
115        }
116
117        return null;
118    }
119
120    /**
121     *  Creates an ETag based on page information. An ETag is unique to each page and version, so it can be used to check if the page has
122     *  changed. Do not assume that the ETag is in any particular format.
123     *  
124     *  @param pageName  The page name for which the ETag should be created.
125     *  @param lastModified  The page last modified date for which the ETag should be created.
126     *  @return A String depiction of an ETag.
127     */
128    public static String createETag( final String pageName, final Date lastModified ) {
129        return Long.toString( pageName.hashCode() ^ lastModified.getTime() );
130    }
131    
132    /**
133     *  If returns true, then should return a 304 (HTTP_NOT_MODIFIED)
134     *
135     *  @param req the HTTP request
136     *  @param pageName the wiki page name to check for
137     *  @param lastModified the last modified date of the wiki page to check for
138     *  @return the result of the check
139     */
140    public static boolean checkFor304( final HttpServletRequest req, final String pageName, final Date lastModified ) {
141        // We'll do some handling for CONDITIONAL GET (and return a 304). If the client has set the following headers, do not try for a 304.
142        //    pragma: no-cache
143        //    cache-control: no-cache
144        if( "no-cache".equalsIgnoreCase( req.getHeader( "Pragma" ) )
145            || "no-cache".equalsIgnoreCase( req.getHeader( "cache-control" ) ) ) {
146            // Wants specifically a fresh copy
147        } else {
148            //  HTTP 1.1 ETags go first
149            final String thisTag = createETag( pageName, lastModified );
150            final String eTag = req.getHeader( "If-None-Match" );
151            
152            if( eTag != null && eTag.equals(thisTag) ) {
153                return true;
154            }
155            
156            //  Next, try if-modified-since
157            final DateFormat rfcDateFormat = new SimpleDateFormat( "EEE, dd MMM yyyy HH:mm:ss z" );
158
159            try {
160                final long ifModifiedSince = req.getDateHeader( "If-Modified-Since" );
161
162                if( ifModifiedSince != -1 ) {
163                    final long lastModifiedTime = lastModified.getTime();
164                    if( lastModifiedTime <= ifModifiedSince ) {
165                        return true;
166                    }
167                } else {
168                    try {
169                        final String s = req.getHeader("If-Modified-Since");
170                        if( s != null ) {
171                            final Date ifModifiedSinceDate = rfcDateFormat.parse( s );
172                            if( lastModified.before( ifModifiedSinceDate ) ) {
173                                return true;
174                            }
175                        }
176                    } catch( final ParseException e ) {
177                        LOG.warn( e.getLocalizedMessage(), e );
178                    }
179                }
180            } catch( final IllegalArgumentException e ) {
181                // Illegal date/time header format.  We fail quietly, and return false.
182                // FIXME: Should really move to ETags.
183            }
184        }
185         
186        return false;
187    }
188
189    /**
190     * Attempts to form a valid URI based on the string given.  Currently it can guess email addresses (mailto:).  If nothing else is given,
191     * it assumes it to be an http:// url.
192     * 
193     * @param uri  URI to take a poke at
194     * @return Possibly a valid URI
195     * @since 2.2.8
196     */
197    public static String guessValidURI( String uri ) {
198        if( uri.indexOf( '@' ) != -1 ) {
199            if( !uri.startsWith( "mailto:" ) ) {
200                // Assume this is an email address
201                uri = "mailto:" + uri;
202            }
203        } else if( notBeginningWithHttpOrHttps( uri ) ) {
204            uri = "http://" + uri;
205        }
206        
207        return uri;
208    }
209
210    static boolean notBeginningWithHttpOrHttps( final String uri ) {
211        return !uri.isEmpty() && !( uri.startsWith("http://" ) || uri.startsWith( "https://" ) );
212    }
213
214    /**
215     *  Returns the query string (the portion after the question mark).
216     *
217     *  @param request The HTTP request to parse.
218     *  @return The query string. If the query string is null, returns an empty string.
219     *  @since 2.1.3 (method moved from WikiEngine on 2.11.0.M6)
220     */
221    public static String safeGetQueryString( final HttpServletRequest request, final Charset contentEncoding ) {
222        if( request == null ) {
223            return "";
224        }
225
226        String res = request.getQueryString();
227        if( res != null ) {
228            res = new String( res.getBytes( StandardCharsets.ISO_8859_1 ), contentEncoding );
229
230            //
231            // Ensure that the 'page=xyz' attribute is removed
232            // FIXME: Is it really the mandate of this routine to do that?
233            //
234            final int pos1 = res.indexOf( "page=" );
235            if( pos1 >= 0 ) {
236                String tmpRes = res.substring( 0, pos1 );
237                final int pos2 = res.indexOf( '&', pos1 ) + 1;
238                if( ( pos2 > 0 ) && ( pos2 < res.length() ) ) {
239                    tmpRes = tmpRes + res.substring( pos2 );
240                }
241                res = tmpRes;
242            }
243        }
244
245        return res;
246    }
247
248    /**
249     * Verifies whether a String represents an IPv4 address. The algorithm is extremely efficient and does not allocate any objects.
250     *
251     * @param name the address to test
252     * @return the result
253     */
254    public static boolean isIPV4Address( final String name ) {
255        if( StringUtils.isEmpty( name ) || name.charAt( 0 ) == DOT || name.charAt( name.length() - 1 ) == DOT ) {
256            return false;
257        }
258
259        final int[] addr = new int[] { 0, 0, 0, 0 };
260        int currentOctet = 0;
261        for( int i = 0; i < name.length(); i++ ) {
262            if( currentOctet > 3 ) {
263                return false;
264            }
265            final int ch = name.charAt( i );
266            final boolean isDigit = ch >= ONE && ch <= NINE;
267            final boolean isDot = ch == DOT;
268            if( !isDigit && !isDot ) {
269                return false;
270            }
271            if( isDigit ) {
272                addr[ currentOctet ] = 10 * addr[ currentOctet ] + ( ch - ONE );
273                if( addr[ currentOctet ] > 255 ) {
274                    return false;
275                }
276            } else if( name.charAt( i - 1 ) == DOT ) {
277                return false;
278            } else {
279                currentOctet++;
280            }
281        }
282        return currentOctet == 3;
283    }
284
285    public static void clearCookie( final HttpServletResponse response, final String cookieName ) {
286        final Cookie cookie = new Cookie( cookieName, "" );
287        cookie.setMaxAge( 0 );
288        response.addCookie( cookie );
289    }

291    /**
292     * Generates an absolute URL based on the given HttpServletRequest and a relative URL.
293     * This method takes into account various headers like X-Forwarded-Host, X-Forwarded-Proto,
294     * and X-Forwarded-Server to construct the absolute URL.
295     *
296     * @param request The HttpServletRequest object, used to obtain scheme, server name, and port.
297     * @param relativeUrl The relative URL to be appended to the base URL. Can be null.
298     * @return The absolute URL as a String.
299     * @since 2.12.2
300     */
301    public static String getAbsoluteUrl(final HttpServletRequest request, final String relativeUrl) {
302        StringBuilder baseUrl = new StringBuilder();
303
304        // Check for proxy headers
305        final String forwardedHost = request.getHeader("X-Forwarded-Host");
306        final String forwardedProto = request.getHeader("X-Forwarded-Proto");
307        final String forwardedServer = request.getHeader("X-Forwarded-Server");
308
309        if (forwardedHost != null && forwardedProto != null) {
310            baseUrl.append(forwardedProto).append("://").append(forwardedHost);
311        } else if (forwardedServer != null && forwardedProto != null) {
312            baseUrl.append(forwardedProto).append("://").append(forwardedServer);
313        } else {
314            // Fallback to HttpServletRequest
315            final String scheme = request.getScheme();
316            final String serverName = request.getServerName();
317            final int port = request.getServerPort();
318
319            baseUrl.append(scheme).append("://").append(serverName);
320
321            // Include port only if it's not the default port for the scheme
322            if ((URIScheme.HTTP.same(scheme) && port != 80)
323                    || (URIScheme.HTTPS.same(scheme) && port != 443)) {
324                baseUrl.append(':');
325                baseUrl.append(port);
326            }
327        }
328
329        if (relativeUrl != null) {
330            baseUrl.append(relativeUrl);
331        }
332
333        return baseUrl.toString();
334    }
335
336
337    /**
338     * Generate an absolute URL based solely on the given HttpServletRequest.
339     * This is a convenience method that calls {@link #getAbsoluteUrl(HttpServletRequest, String)}
340     * with a null relative URL.
341     *
342     * @param request The HttpServletRequest object, used to obtain scheme, server name, and port.
343     * @return The absolute URL as a String.
344     * @see #getAbsoluteUrl(HttpServletRequest, String)
345     * @since 2.12.2
346     */
347    public static String getAbsoluteUrl(final HttpServletRequest request) {
348        return getAbsoluteUrl(request, null);
349    }
